risk: Counts drift: a requested two-by-five grid gave 25 to 28 tiles. One straight row of separate tiles is the rewrite; if both candidates drift, keep the vector (art direction 5.1).

copy.anchor: Earn your first customers: win your first customers with personal outreach, a scoped pilot, fast onboarding and a conversation log that records why people said yes or no. (/playbooks/earn-your-first-customers/)
copy.convey: One account at a time, each a separate tile.
copy.avoid: Customers as proof (claim C-13), a logo wall, a funnel, a chart, people.

object.subject: Overhead still life of one straight row of matte six-sided hexagon tiles in blue and white on a pale surface, each tile separate with open space around it, even spacing.
object.accent: the last tile in the row, in amber glass

prompts.object: Editorial still life photograph of a hand-built tabletop model made of paper, card, matte ceramic and brushed steel, photographed as a physical object on a plain pale surface, soft north-window light with long gentle shadows, 50mm lens, shallow depth of field, matte film grade with lifted whites. Overhead still life of one straight row of matte six-sided hexagon tiles in blue and white on a pale surface, each tile separate with open space around it, even spacing. Subject centred with a quiet margin around it. Color palette: crisp white and pale mist-blue surfaces, deep blue and slate, soft grey. There is exactly one amber object in the frame: the last tile in the row, in amber glass. All other objects are white, grey, blue or slate. No text, no logos, no writing.
